attributes.body:
など is an adverbial particle that is used to express that something is being presented as an example, but that other things in the same category also exist. In this way, it is regularly translated as 'such as', 'things like', or 'and so on'.

など may be used after nouns, to describe that (A) is being presented as an example from within a group. Alternatively, など can be followed by の (B), to show that (A) is only one example from within a broader category related to (B).

など is regularly seen in its kanji form, 等（など）. This kanji itself has a similar meaning to 'etc' in English.

Fun Fact

The kanji for 等（など） is also used in the pluralizing suffix, ら. Due to this, we can see that this kanji is regularly utilized to highlight something that exists as part of a larger group.

In the first sentence, など presents (A) as being part of a larger group of similar things. This is exactly the same thing that happens in the second sentence with ら.

Fun Fact

など is also sometimes written as なんか, and has an interchangeable meaning in many situations. However, なんか will never use the kanji form of 等（など）.

attributes.source: [DBJG] A Dictionary of Basic Japanese Grammar

attributes.body: Both なんか・なんて and など can be used to give examples, like '(A) and so on' or 'things like (A)', but they differ in nuance and formality. など is neutral and used in both speech and writing. なんか・なんて are more casual and often carry a dismissive or belittling tone, like '(A) and whatever' or 'unimportant things like (A)'.

attributes.body: だの and など are similar in that both are used to list examples. They differ in that だの will often explicitly list multiple examples, while など can be used with a singular example to suggest 'and things like that'. Also だの often is used in statements with a negative implication, while など is more neutral and has no such limitations.

attributes.body: といった and など both give examples, but differ in usage. といった appears in the form AといったB, meaning '(B) such as (A),' e.g. サッカーといったスポーツ ('sports like soccer'). など can be used similarly as AなどのB, but also stands alone, e.g. サッカーなどが好き ('I like soccer and similar things.').

attributes.body: など and とか～とか both list examples, but differ in nuance and structure. など usually follows a single noun or ends a list, implying the items are representative, like '(A) and so on' or 'things like (A).' とか～とか follows each noun and emphasizes specific, individual examples, like '(A) and (B), for example'.
